prompt.en: To build the lift, say where each piece goes: up with the floats, or down on the sand.
prompt.ar: لِتَبْنِيَ الرَّافِعَة، قُلْ أَيْنَ تَذْهَبُ كُلُّ قِطْعَة: فَوْقُ مَعَ العَوَّامَات، أَمْ تَحْتُ عَلَى الرَّمْل.

hint1.en: Not quite. Watch what it did when you let go.
hint1.ar: لَيْسَ تَمَامًا. اُنْظُرْ مَاذَا فَعَلَتْ حِينَ تَرَكْتَهَا.

hint2.en: Size is not the answer. A whole log rides up, and so does a thread of kelp.
hint2.ar: الحَجْمُ لَيْسَ هُوَ الجَوَاب. جِذْعٌ كَامِلٌ يَطْفُو، وَخَيْطُ عُشْبٍ يَطْفُو كَذَلِك.

model.en: This is where it ends up. Now you send one.
model.ar: هُنَا يَنْتَهِي بِهَا المَطَاف. أَرْسِلْ أَنْتَ وَاحِدَةً الآن.

success.en: Floats on top, weights below. That is a lift.
success.ar: العَوَّامَاتُ فَوْق، وَالأَثْقَالُ تَحْت. هَذِهِ رَافِعَة.

payload._comment: An experiment, not a quiz about one. The child has to predict — buoyancy is the one property here that cannot be seen, only reasoned about — and then the object answers. A float dropped on the sand drifts back up, in front of them, which is a better correction than any sound: it tells them WHAT THE THING IS, which is something they can use on the next piece.
payload._castComment: Cross-balanced against size in BOTH directions, and the second direction is the one that is easy to forget. Driftwood, a coconut and a crate are big and float, so 'big things sink' fails immediately. But a cast whose floaters are all big still lets a child run 'small things sink' undefeated for the whole round and score full marks on a rule that is false — so kelp is in here as a small thing that rides up, and a stone and a chain are big things that do not. Neither naive rule survives a single round.
payload._heldConstantComment: heldConstant is deliberately EMPTY. Sorting activities normally hold the other attributes still so the target one is the only thing varying — but here size has to vary, and vary against the answer, or the round teaches a rule that is not true. Claiming size as held constant would be a lie the validator catches, correctly.
